answer.short: Acute: isosceles C; equilateral I, B; scalene E, G. Right: isosceles F; equilateral none; scalene A. Obtuse: isosceles D; equilateral none; scalene H.
answer.worked:
A: right-angled and scalene—one angle is $90^{\circ}$ and the angles are unequal.

B: acute and equilateral—all three angles are $60^{\circ}$.

C: acute and isosceles—two angles are $70^{\circ}$.

D: obtuse and isosceles—one angle is $130^{\circ}$ and two angles are $25^{\circ}$.

E: acute and scalene—the angles $72^{\circ}$, $74^{\circ}$ and $34^{\circ}$ are all acute and unequal.

F: right-angled and isosceles—one angle is $90^{\circ}$ and two angles are $45^{\circ}$.

G: acute and scalene—the angles $61^{\circ}$, $59^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ are all acute and unequal.

H: obtuse and scalene—one angle is $92^{\circ}$ and all three angles are unequal.

I: by symmetry, the reflected base angles are both $60^{\circ}$ and the vertex half-angles are both $30^{\circ}$. Hence all three angles are $60^{\circ}$, so triangle I is acute and equilateral.

$$\begin{align*}b+56&=90\\b&=34^\circ\\c+34+90&=180\\c+124&=180\\c&=56^\circ\\d+56&=90\\d&=34^\circ\\a&=b=34^\circ\\e&=c=56^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded triangle XWZ with Y on the horizontal base XZ and internal segment WY. Single ticks identify WX = XY; double ticks identify WY = YZ. The angle at X is labelled 2x without a degree symbol.
spec.mathematics: X, Y and Z are collinear in that order. WX = XY and WY = YZ create two isosceles triangles. Angle WYZ is exterior to triangle XWY.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated angle expressions appear.

answer.short: $\angle XWY=\angle XYW=90-x$; $\angle WYZ=90+x$; $\angle YWZ=\angle WZY=45-\frac{x}{2}$. The whole triangle has $\angle WXZ=2x$, $\angle XWZ=135-\frac{3x}{2}$ and $\angle WZX=45-\frac{x}{2}$.
answer.worked:
Since $WX=XY$, the base angles of $\triangle XWY$ are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle XWY=\angle XYW&=\frac{180-2x}{2}\\&=90-x\end{aligned}$$
By the exterior angle theorem in $\triangle XWY$,
$$\begin{aligned}\angle WYZ&=2x+(90-x)\\&=90+x\end{aligned}$$
Since $WY=YZ$, the base angles of $\triangle WYZ$ are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle YWZ=\angle WZY&=\frac{180-(90+x)}{2}\\&=45-\frac{x}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Adding the adjacent angles at $W$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}\angle XWZ&=(90-x)+\left(45-\frac{x}{2}\right)\\&=135-\frac{3x}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Also, $\angle WXZ=2x$ and $\angle WZX=\angle WZY=45-\frac{x}{2}$.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with horizontal AB and DC; DC extends through C to E. BE completes triangle BCE. Matching double ticks mark AD and BE. Angle DAB is labelled 120 degrees. All five vertex labels are retained, with no parallel arrows or shading.

answer.short: $BC=AD=BE$ and $\angle BCE=60^{\circ}$. Hence $\angle BEC=\angle CBE=60^{\circ}$, so $\triangle BCE$ is equilateral.
answer.worked:
$$\angle BCD=\angle DAB=120^{\circ}$$
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.

$$\angle BCE=180^{\circ}-120^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.

$$BC=AD$$
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.

The diagram marks $AD=BE$, so $BC=AD=BE$ and $\triangle BCE$ is isosceles.

$$\angle BEC=\angle BCE=60^{\circ}$$
Angles opposite equal sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.

$$\angle CBE=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$$
The angles of a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.

Therefore $\triangle BCE$ is equilateral, since all three angles are $60^{\circ}$.

inlines.text: The length of the diagonals of a rhombus is 24 cm and 18 cm.
Find the length of each side of the rhombus.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, forming four right-angled triangles. Each triangle has perpendicular sides of $24\div2=12\text{ cm}$ and $18\div2=9\text{ cm}$. Each rhombus side is a hypotenuse. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}l^2&=12^2+9^2\\l^2&=144+81\\l^2&=225\\l&=\sqrt{225}\\l&=15\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Each resulting right-angled triangle has hypotenuse $5\text{ cm}$ and one shorter side of length $4\text{ cm}$. Let $l$ be half the unknown diagonal and $d$ its full length.

spec.mathematics: The rhombus's lower-right interior angle and the triangle's 27° angle are supplementary. Opposite rhombus angles are equal and adjacent rhombus angles are supplementary.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and pronumerals appear; calculated values are answer-controlled.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}e+27^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\e&=153^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The four equal sides identify a rhombus. Opposite angles are equal, so $f=153^{\circ}$. Adjacent angles are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}g+153^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\g&=27^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Opposite angles are equal, so $h=27^{\circ}$.

spec.description: An unshaded isosceles triangle adjoining an isosceles trapezium. spec.mathematics: The triangle's two base angles are 26°, giving its remaining angle as 128°. The straight continuation makes d supplementary to 128°. The parallel sides and equal legs identify an isosceles trapezium, whose lower base angles are 128°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and pronumerals appear; calculated values are answer-controlled.

answer.worked:
The triangle has two equal sides, so its other base angle is $26^{\circ}$. Let its angle at the upper shared vertex be $t$.
$$\begin{align*}t+26^{\circ}+26^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\t+52^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\t&=128^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}d+128^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\d&=52^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The quadrilateral is an isosceles trapezium. Its upper base angles are equal, and angles along either leg are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}e+52^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\e&=128^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
The left interior angle is $360^\circ-250^\circ=110^\circ$ (angles at a point). The right interior angle is $180^\circ-140^\circ=40^\circ$ (angles on a straight line).
The other two interior angles of the kite are equal. Let each be $b$.
$$\begin{align*}110+40+b+b&=360\\2b+150&=360\\2b&=210\\b&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
The required reflex angle is $x=360^\circ-105^\circ=255^\circ$.

Angle sum of the lower triangle:

Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be the interior angles adjacent to $c$, $b$ and $a$, respectively. Angles around each vertex sum to $360^{\circ}$:

b+y&=360^{\circ}\\

$$\begin{align*}
a+b+c&=1080^{\circ}-(x+y+z)\\
a+b+c&=1080^{\circ}-180^{\circ}\\
a+b+c&=900^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$

answer.short: $x=25$. The angles are $70^\circ$, $110^\circ$, $70^\circ$ and $110^\circ$ in clockwise order from the top-left. Adjacent angles sum to $180^\circ$, proving both pairs of opposite sides parallel by the converse of the co-interior angle property. Hence the shape is a parallelogram.
answer.worked:
The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
(3x-5)+(4x+10)+(5x-15)+(2x+20)&=360\\
14x+10&=360\\
14x&=350\\
x&=25
\end{align*}$$
Substituting $x=25$ gives the top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right angles as $70^\circ$, $110^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $70^\circ$, respectively.
$$\begin{align*}
(5x-15)+(2x+20)&=180\\
(3x-5)+(4x+10)&=180\\
(3x-5)+(5x-15)&=180\\
(4x+10)+(2x+20)&=180
\end{align*}$$
The first two sums show that the left and right sides are parallel. The last two show that the top and bottom sides are parallel. In each case, co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$, so the lines are parallel by the converse of the co-interior angle property. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel; therefore the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

content.prompt: Prove that $\angle LNO = 90^\circ + y$

spec.description: Isosceles triangle LMN with apex L above horizontal MN, matching single side ticks, an apex angle arc labelled 2y, and MN extended through N to O.
mathematics: M, N and O are collinear in that order
The interior angle MLN is labelled 2y without a degree symbol
Angle LNO is the exterior angle at N
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no derived base or exterior angles are supplied.

answer.short: $\angle LNM=\dfrac{180^\circ-2y}{2}=90^\circ-y$ because the base angles are equal. Hence $\angle LNO=180^\circ-(90^\circ-y)=90^\circ+y$.
answer.worked:
The base angles of isosceles triangle $LMN$ are equal, and its angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
\angle LNM &= \frac{180^\circ-2y}{2} \\
\angle LNM &= 90^\circ-y
\end{align*}$$
Adjacent angles on the straight line $MNO$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
\angle LNM+\angle LNO &= 180^\circ \\
90^\circ-y+\angle LNO &= 180^\circ \\
\angle LNO &= 90^\circ+y
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Find the value of $x$ in these diagrams.

spec.description: Unshaded house-shaped pentagon with five matching single equality ticks, two bottom right-angle squares, and red dashed segments from the roof apex to both bottom corners. The angle between the dashed segments is labelled x degrees.
spec.mathematics: Both upright sides are perpendicular to the base and equal to it. Their upper endpoints are separated by the base length, so the equal roof edges form an equilateral triangle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source unknown x is visible; no numerical answer or added construction is printed.

answer.short: $x=30^{\circ}$. Join the upper ends of the vertical sides to form an equilateral roof triangle.
answer.worked:
Join the upper ends of the vertical sides. The lower quadrilateral is a square, so the new segment equals each roof edge. The roof triangle is therefore equilateral, with each angle $60^{\circ}$.

Each angle where a vertical side meets a roof edge is $90^{\circ}+60^{\circ}=150^{\circ}$. Each side triangle formed by a red dashed segment is isosceles, since its two outer edges are equal. Its two base angles are
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{base angle}&=\frac{180^{\circ}-150^{\circ}}{2}\\
&=15^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$
The two dashed segments split the roof apex angle into $15^{\circ}$, $x$ and $15^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{aligned}
x+15^{\circ}+15^{\circ}&=60^{\circ}\\
x&=30^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Unshaded square-shaped outer quadrilateral. All four sides and both solid segments from the bottom corners to the interior apex have matching single ticks. Red dashed segments join the interior apex to both top corners. Their upper angle is labelled x degrees. No right-angle markers are added.
spec.mathematics: The lower triangle is equilateral and the equal outer sides establish a rhombus. Its adjacent bottom angles are supplementary. The two side triangles are isosceles, and their angles at the interior apex total 150 degrees. Angles around that apex give x = 150 degrees without requiring a square designation.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source unknown x is visible; no supplied numerical answer or inferred right-angle markers are printed.

answer.short: $x=150^{\circ}$. Use supplementary adjacent angles of the rhombus and the equal base angles of the two side triangles.
answer.worked:
The outer quadrilateral is a rhombus because its four sides are equal. The lower triangle is equilateral because its three sides are equal, so each of its angles is $60^{\circ}$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be the angles between an outer side and a solid interior segment at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners. Adjacent angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so
$$\begin{aligned}
(a+60^{\circ})+(b+60^{\circ})&=180^{\circ}\\
a+b&=60^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$
Each side triangle is isosceles, since its outer side and solid interior segment are equal. Their angles at the interior apex therefore total
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{180^{\circ}-a}{2}+\frac{180^{\circ}-b}{2}&=\frac{360^{\circ}-(a+b)}{2}\\
&=150^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$
Using the angles around the interior apex,
$$\begin{aligned}
x+150^{\circ}+60^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\
x&=150^{\circ}.
\end{aligned}$$

entries.description:
Syllabus Content

MA4-GEO-C-01 identifies and applies the properties of triangles and quadrilaterals to solve problems

Classify triangles according to their side and angle properties
• Label triangles using appropriate text and symbols
• Classify and describe types of triangles based on their properties, including acute-angled, right-angled, obtuse-angled, equilateral, isosceles and scalene triangles

Classify quadrilaterals and describe their properties
• Identify quadrilaterals using naming conventions
• Distinguish between convex and non-convex quadrilaterals
• Verify and describe the properties of the special quadrilaterals which include parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, squares, trapeziums and kites
• Identify and label the properties of the special quadrilaterals using appropriate conventions
• Classify quadrilaterals based on their properties
• Justify why some quadrilaterals may be classified as more than one type of quadrilateral

Apply the properties of triangles and quadrilaterals
• Prove that the interior angle sum of a triangle is 180° with or without digital tools
• Prove that any exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the 2 interior opposite angles
• Apply the angle sum of a triangle to prove that the angle sum of a quadrilateral is 360°
• Apply the properties of triangles and quadrilaterals to determine unknown sides and angles to solve problems, giving reasons

NAPLAN B+
The diagram shows a parallelogram ABCD. Prove that ΔBCE is equilateral.

presentation.subtitle: NAPLAN B+
presentation.responseSpace: Open working space beneath the diagram for a proof with reasons.

entries.description: Parallelogram ABCD with A upper left, B upper right, D lower left and C below and left of B. DC extends through C to E on the right. Segment BE completes triangle BCE. AB and DCE are horizontal. AD and BE carry matching double equality ticks. The interior angle DAB is marked 120° with an arc. All five vertex labels are present. No parallel-arrow markings are shown.

presentation.placement: Below the question text, before the proof response space.

entries.description: Visible blue supplied proof, separated from the unsolved student prompt.

expectedAnswer.worked:
∠BCD = 120° because opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
∠ECB = 60° because angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
BC = AD because opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.
The diagram marks AD = BE, so BC = BE and ΔBCE is isosceles.
Therefore ∠BCE = ∠BEC = 60° because angles opposite equal sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.
∠CBE = 180° − 60° − 60° = 60° by the angle sum of a triangle.
Therefore ΔBCE is equilateral because all its angles are 60°.
expectedAnswer.short: ΔBCE is equilateral: BC = AD = BE and ∠BCE = 60°, so ∠BEC = ∠CBE = 60°.

entries.description:

entries.description: Visible blue supplied explanation and calculation.

expectedAnswer.worked:
The diagonals form four right-angled triangles where the perpendicular sides are 12 cm and 9 cm.
The hypotenuse is the side length of the rhombus.
l = √(12² + 9²) = 15 cm.

entries.description:

presentation.responseSpace: Open working space below the prompt for finding half the unknown diagonal and doubling it.

entries.description: Visible blue supplied explanation, intermediate calculation and final answer.

expectedAnswer.worked:
The diagonals form four right-angled triangles where the hypotenuse is 5 cm and one of the shorter sides is 4 cm.
The other diagonal is double the other side length.
l = √(5² − 4²) = 3 cm.
The other diagonal is 2 × 3 = 6 cm.
